books.section: Topic 3.13 Continuity and Change in Period 3

stimulus.text:
| | 1763 | 1800 |
|---|---|---|
| Ruler | A king in London, with royal governors in the colonies | An elected president and Congress under a written Constitution |
| National legislature | None elected by Americans; Parliament made the laws | Congress, with a House elected by voters and a Senate chosen by state legislatures |
| Voting | Limited to men with property in most colonies | Still limited to men with property in most states |

New Jersey's constitution of 1776 let “all inhabitants” worth £50 vote, so some women voted there. Laws in 1790 and 1797 made that plain. In 1807 the legislature limited the vote to white men.
stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 5 and 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Chapter 11. New Jersey voting: Smithsonian Magazine and Tufts University, “A New Nation Votes.”

source: original; table compiled from Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 5 and 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Chapter 11; New Jersey voting from Smithsonian Magazine and Tufts University, “A New Nation Votes.”
stem: Which row of the table shows a continuity rather than a change?

options.text: The voting row: it was limited to men with property in both years.
The ruler row: a king in 1763, an elected president in 1800.
options.misconception: The ruler row changed completely, from a king to an elected president.

options.text: The legislature row: no elected body in 1763, Congress in 1800.
options.misconception: The legislature row changed completely, from none elected to Congress.

options.text: All three rows show a change, with nothing staying the same.
options.misconception: The voting row stayed the same, so not all three rows changed.

rationales.A: Voting was limited to men with property in 1763 and still limited in 1800, so this row stayed the same.
rationales.B: The ruler row changed completely, from a king to an elected president.
rationales.C: The legislature row changed completely, from none elected to Congress.
rationales.D: The voting row stayed the same, so not all three rows changed.
rationales.general:
1. Check the ruler row: king in 1763, elected president in 1800. That changed.
2. Check the legislature row: none elected by Americans in 1763, Congress in 1800. That changed too.
3. Check the voting row: limited to men with property in both years. That stayed the same.
4. So the voting row is the continuity.
Remember: a continuity is a row where the two columns match.
